patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — 8x8 documents a broader use-case set; Fastmail is narrower/specialist.

Comparison thesis: General-purpose vs specialist. Choose 8x8 only if your buying job matches “Global UCaaS + contact-centre platform (8x8 Work / X Series) — Work X2 research floor ~$24” rather than Fastmail's shape. Choose Fastmail only if your buying job matches “Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom domains and shared addre” rather than 8x8's shape. Workflow advantage: 8x8 leans business-phone, sales-calling; Fastmail leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — 8x8 documents a broader use-case set; Fastmail is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: 8x8 is Global UCaaS + contact-centre platform (8x8 Work / X Series) — Work X2 research floor ~$24/user/month annual; CC tiers custom/higher.; Fastmail is Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom domains and shared addresses — Business Basic from $3/user/month annual; a.
- Company-size focus: 8x8 (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Fastmail (micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: 8x8-leaning business-phone, sales-calling, contact-center vs Fastmail-leaning —.
- Researched limits: 8x8 — Published seat floors are medium confidence — first-party pricing often bot/quote gated; Fastmail — Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications.

Limitations — 8x8: Published seat floors are medium confidence — first-party pricing often bot/quote gated; Mandatory regulatory/service fees frequently sit on top of list seats; Fastmail: Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications; Shared addresses, shared calendars and the shared address book require Standard or above.

Poor-fit cases: 8x8 is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Published seat floors are medium confidence — first-party pricing often bot/quote gated · Fastmail is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications · Avoid 8x8 if you actually need Fastmail's motion (Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom domains and sh)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
